title.en: Twelve killed as Polish bus veers off Hungarian motorway
title.zh: 波兰巴士在匈牙利高速公路翻车，十二人死亡

summary.en: A tourist bus overturned on a Hungarian motorway in the early hours of Sunday morning, killing twelve people and seriously injuring dozens more.
summary.zh: 周日凌晨，一辆旅游巴士在匈牙利高速公路上翻车，造成十二人死亡，另有数十人受重伤。

body.en:
Twelve people were killed and dozens more injured when a bus carrying Polish pilgrims veered off a Hungarian motorway and into a ditch.

Police said the bus overturned after coming off the M3 motorway, which connects Hungary's capital Budapest with the north-eastern city of Nyíregyháza, at around 01:00 local time on Sunday (23:00 GMT on Saturday).

Officers believe the driver fell asleep at the wheel. He has been taken into custody.

Thirty-five out of the 57 passengers and two drivers onboard have been rescued by firefighters so far, state media reports.

Emergency services had been attempting to lift the rear axle of the 24-tonne bus to remove the people trapped underneath before cranes arrived to lift the whole vehicle, according to Hungarian news agency MTI.

Hungary's ambulance service said it had treated one person with life-threatening injuries, nine people with serious injuries and a further 37 people with minor injuries.

The country's Prime Minister Péter Magyar offered his "sincere condolences" to the families of the victims and wished those injured a speedy recovery.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk echoed his sentiments, adding he had decided to send a "special" Polish aircraft with foreign ministry officials and medical services.

The bus had been returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina, and had been carrying pilgrims from Poland's southernmost region of Podkarpacie, according to Polish news agency PAP.

Poland's Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said his Hungarian counterpart had told him police had already begun questioning the bus driver.
body.zh: 一辆波兰旅游巴士冲出匈牙利高速公路并驶入沟渠，造成十二人死亡、数十人受伤。 警方表示，这辆巴士于当地时间周日 01:00 左右（格林威治标准时间周六 23:00）驶出连接匈牙利首都布达佩斯和东北部城市尼赖吉哈佐的 M3 高速公路后翻车。 警方认为司机在方向盘上睡着了。他已被拘留。 据官方媒体报道，目前机上 57 名乘客和两名司机中的 35 人已被消防员救出。 据 MTI 通讯社报道，紧急服务部门一直在尝试抬起这辆 24 吨巴士的后轴，以将被困在车底下的人转移出去，然后起重机才到达，将整个车辆吊起。 匈牙利救护车服务部门表示，已救治一名危及生命的伤者、九名重伤者和另外 37 名轻伤者。 该国总理彼得·马扎尔向遇难者家属表示“诚挚的哀悼”，并祝愿伤者早日康复。

In moments of such deep pain, we hold onto the promise that Yahweh will one day wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. This hope reminds us that even in the darkest times, there is a future where suffering is ultimately...
reflection.zh: 这场悲惨事故中生命的骤然逝去和严重的伤势给许多人带来了深切的悲痛。在如此深重的痛苦时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟的应许，他将有一天擦去我们所有的眼泪，不再有死亡、悲哀、哭号和疼痛。这个盼望提醒我们，即使在最黑暗的时刻，也有一个最终战胜苦难的未来。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Five killed as Russia launches fresh aerial attacks across Ukraine
title.zh: 俄罗斯对乌克兰发动新一轮空袭，造成五人死亡

summary.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has accused Russia of targeting civilian infrastructure in fresh aerial attacks that killed five people, while Moscow reported hitting a warehouse.
summary.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基指责俄罗斯在造成五人死亡的新一轮空袭中，瞄准了民用基础设施，而莫斯科则报告称击中了一个仓库。

body.en:
At least five people have been killed and more than 10 injured in Ukraine in the latest wave of Russian strikes, officials have said.

The attacks caused fires across the capital, Kyiv, including at a book market, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, accusing Russia of targeting civilian infrastructure.

Meanwhile, Moscow's mayor said about 600 Ukrainian drones were launched towards the city overnight. A warehouse belonging to Russian online retailer Wildberries was hit. Seven people have died across Russia, officials said.

Russia has intensified aerial attacks across Ukraine in recent weeks, while Kyiv has stepped up attacks on Russian logistics hubs, aiming to disrupt military supplies.

Air-raid sirens have sounded four times since Saturday night in Kyiv. At least six people, including a child, were reportedly injured, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.

The mayor of Kryvyi Rih said a 44-year-old man earlier reported missing had been found dead in rubble. Another person was killed and 14 workers of a steel plant were wounded there.

Two people in their 60s were killed when a house was destroyed in Zaporizhzhia, while a person was also killed in Sumy, according to the Ukrainian president.

Zelensky said the cities of Kremenchuk and Kryvyi Rih were hit by ballistic missiles, adding: "Wherever the Russians can reach with their ballistic missiles, they strike civilian infrastructure."

Russia said its attacks on Kyiv on Saturday night targeted a FirePoint facility producing parts for Ukrainian Flamingo missiles and a factory making components for drones.

A book market in the city's Pochayna district was damaged in the strikes. Burnt books could be seen lying on the ground, while firefighters continue to douse the flames.

Looking through the rubble, she told the BBC: "All these books in the street were from my husband's stall in the market - I recognise them on the floor."

Vinyl store owner Luba, 42, said she has lost 500,000 hryvnias (£8,262) worth of stock.

"This business was my baby - many of the vinyls destroyed were rare and irreplaceable," she told the BBC. "I want Russia to disappear from this Earth."

The country's defence ministry also said it hit the Kremenchuk oil refinery in Poltava region, which it said supplied fuel to the Ukrainian military.

Moscow said it struck a steelworks in Kryvyi Rih it said had been making weapons components.

Russia also said it hit a dry cargo vessel near Odesa, claiming it had been carrying military equipment.

Zelensky said 13 regions had come under attack this week, with Russia launching more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided aerial bombs and 62 missiles.

In Russia, air defences intercepted and destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones, according to its defence ministry.

reflection.en: The ongoing aerial attacks and loss of life in Ukraine remind us of the devastating reality of war and the profound human cost. In such moments of conflict and despair, we hold onto the hope that Yahweh ultimately has the power to bring all wars to an end. This promise offers solace and a vision of a future where peace prevails.
reflection.zh: 乌克兰持续的空袭和生命损失提醒我们战争的毁灭性现实和沉重的人类代价。在这样的冲突和绝望时刻，我们坚信雅伟最终有能力结束一切战争。这个应许带来慰藉，并描绘了一个和平盛行的未来。

verse.textEn: He makes wars cease to the ends of the earth; he breaks the bow and shatters the spear.

title.en: Destroyed crops, riverbed cyclists and a ‘Rock of Starvation’: how drought has devastated the Danube
title.zh: 农作物被毁、河床裸露和“饥饿之石”：干旱如何摧毁多瑙河

summary.en: The Danube River is experiencing a severe drought, causing widespread devastation. Crops have been destroyed, riverbeds are exposed, and some residents are struggling to find drinking water, with a historic “Rock of Starvation” now visible.
summary.zh: 多瑙河正经历严重干旱，造成大范围破坏。农作物被毁，河床裸露，一些居民难以获得饮用水，一块历史性的“饥饿之石”也已显现。

body.en: The Guardian travelled 100 miles along the EU’s longest river, where some residents are struggling to secure drinking water For centuries, the rock was seen as a warning. When it began to emerge from the Danube, beneath Gellért Hill in Budapest, it meant the river had fallen so low that floating mills could no longer operate, crops were probably failing, and hunger would almost certainly follow. That is why, in the Hungarian capital, where over time the boulder became little more than a legend, it was named Ínség-szikla – the Rock of Starvation. Today, amid record-low water levels on the Danube, the rock has not only emerged from the water, but surfaced almost in its entirety, along with the sandy riverbed on which it rests, astonishing geologists and government scientists sent to examine it. And, much as the rock was said to warn, Hungary is now facing an unprecedented energy crisis that has forced the country to shut down all but one of its Danube-cooled nuclear reactors for the first time in 44 years. body.zh: 《卫报》沿着欧盟最长的河流行驶了 100 英里，那里的一些居民正在努力获取饮用水。几个世纪以来，这块岩石被视为一种警告。当它开始从布达佩斯盖勒特山下的多瑙河中涌出时，这意味着河流水位已经下降到浮动磨坊无法再运转，庄稼可能歉收，饥饿几乎肯定会随之而来。这就是为什么在匈牙利首都，随着时间的推移，这块巨石已成为一个传奇，它被命名为Ínség-szikla——饥饿之石。如今，在多瑙河水位创历史新低的情况下，这块岩石不仅从水中露出来，而且几乎整个连同它所在的沙质河床一起浮出水面，令派去检查它的地质学家和政府科学家感到惊讶。而且，正如据说这块岩石所警告的那样，匈牙利现在正面临着一场前所未有的能源危机，迫使该国 44 年来首次关闭了多瑙河冷却核反应堆，只保留了一座。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The devastating drought along the Danube reminds us of life's fragility when essential resources dwindle. Even when fields yield no food and supplies are scarce, the prophet Habakkuk teaches us to find joy in Yahweh. This perspective encourages a deep trust that sustains hope even in the face of profound hardship.
reflection.zh: 多瑙河沿岸毁灭性的干旱提醒我们，当基本资源枯竭时，生命是多么脆弱。即使田地不产粮食，供应稀缺，先知哈巴谷也教导我们要在雅伟里喜乐。这种视角鼓励我们建立一种深刻的信靠，即使面对巨大的困境，也能维系希望。

verse.textEn: Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines... yet I will rejoice in Yahweh.
verse.textZh: 虽然无花果树不发旺，葡萄树不结果……然而，我要因雅伟欢欣。

title.en: Angela Rayner moves to protect pubs from being turned into houses or offices
title.zh: 安吉拉·雷纳采取行动保护酒吧免遭改建为住宅或办公室

summary.en: Angela Rayner, the housing secretary, is introducing new planning laws in England to protect pubs from being converted into housing or offices. Developers will now be required to demonstrate that there is no viable alternative to save a pub before any such conversion can proceed.
summary.zh: 住房大臣安吉拉·雷纳正准备在英格兰推出新的规划法，以保护酒吧免遭改建为住宅或办公室。根据新规定，开发商必须证明没有其他办法可以保留酒吧，才能进行此类改建。

body.en: Housing secretary says developers will have to prove there’s no way to save pub, as she prepares planning shakeup All pubs will get protection from being turned into housing or offices under a shakeup of planning laws in England to be presented by Angela Rayner this week. The housing secretary will publish a new national planning policy framework aimed at loosening planning laws even further to help build 3m homes by the end of the parliament. Continue reading...

title.en: Bus crash in Hungary kills at least 12
title.zh: 匈牙利巴士坠毁，至少12人死亡

summary.en: Police have arrested the driver of a bus that crashed in Hungary, killing at least 12 people. Reports indicated the bus was carrying Polish pilgrims.
summary.zh: 警方表示，一辆在匈牙利坠毁的巴士司机已被逮捕，事故造成至少12人死亡。据报道，该巴士载有波兰朝圣者。

body.en:
Police say they have arrested the driver of a bus that crashed in Hungary, killing at least 12 people. The bus was carrying Polish pilgrims, media report.

At least 12 people have died after a Polish coach crashed into a ditch and overturned in eastern Hungary , police said on Sunday.

According to emergency services, 47 people were injured in the incident, 10 seriously.

The accident occurred on the M3 motorway near Mezokeresztes, around 140 kilometers (87 miles) east of Budapest, according to police in the district capital, Miskolc. 

Police said they believe the driver fell asleep at the wheel during the overnight journey into Sunday. He was subsequently arrested.

Poland's PAP news agency reported that the bus had been carrying a group of pilgrims from Podkarpackie province in the far southeast of Poland .

The group, said to number 59 people, including two drivers, had been returning from Bosnia-Herzegovina , PAP said. 

Hungary's National Directorate for Disaster Management said that several of the passengers had been trapped under the vehicle when it overturned.

  Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar has voiced his condolences to the families of the crash victims in a Facebook message and thanked emergency and rescue services.

 Polish President Karol Nawrocki said he was deeply shaken. "In the face of this unimaginable tragedy, which affects us all, my thoughts and prayers go out to the families and loved ones of the victims," the 43-year-old wrote on X.

title.en: Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots after downing fighter jets
title.zh: 卡塔尔否认在击落战斗机后抓获三名伊朗飞行员

summary.en: Iran claims they have been held since Qatar downed two fighter jets at the start of the US-Iran war.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Iran has called for the release of three pilots it said were captured by Qatar after two of its fighter jets were hit by air defences during a military operation at the start of the US-Iran war.

In a letter to the head of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Iran's Brig Gen Mohammad Bagherzadeh claimed the pilots - Javad Salehi, Abdul Majid Dashtian and Imran Behroshian - had been held captive for six months.

He said the body of a fourth pilot, Majid Kazemi, had been returned after he was killed in the same operation on 2 March 2026 - the third day of the war.

Qatar "categorically denied" Iran's claims and said it was "surprised by these misleading statements".

Bagherzadeh said the three pilots had been captured by Qatar after they ejected from their jets during a combat mission targeting a Qatari military base.

In the letter to ICRC chief Mirjana Spoljaric, published by Iranian media, he accused Qatar of violating "the inalienable rights of these prisoners, contrary to all international laws and regulations".

The letter also claimed the three pilots had not been allowed to meet or contact their families.

Qatar's foreign affairs spokesperson Majed Mohammed Al Ansari said contact had been made with the pilots "after they violated Qatari airspace", but that it had not received a response.

"The necessary measures were taken to defend our territory in accordance with international law," he added in a statement on X.

Al Ansari said Qatar's search and rescue teams "carried out their duties to the fullest extent in searching for the pilots' remains", adding the Gulf nation had contacted Iran "co-ordinate the handover of the remains of one of the pilots that were recovered".

Bagerzadeh later told the semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday that Qatar should allow an Iranian fact-finding team into the country to investigate what had happened, claiming one had been denied entry for months.

Al Ansari said an invitation for an Iranian team to visit Qatar to review the findings of its search and rescue operation had been extended in April but Tehran had yet to respond.
body.zh: 伊朗呼吁释放三名飞行员，据称是在美伊战争开始时的一次军事行动中，其两架战斗机被防空系统击中后被卡塔尔俘虏的。 伊朗准将穆罕默德·巴格尔扎德在致红十字国际委员会主席的一封信中声称，这三名飞行员——贾瓦德·萨利希、阿卜杜勒·马吉德·达什蒂安和伊姆兰·贝赫罗希安——已被关押了六个月。 他说，第四名飞行员马吉德·卡泽米 (Majid Kazemi) 的尸体已于 2026 年 3 月 2 日（即战争的第三天）在同一行动中丧生后被归还。 卡塔尔“断然否认”伊朗的说法，并表示“对这些误导性言论感到惊讶”。 巴格扎德表示，这三名飞行员在执行针对卡塔尔军事基地的战斗任务时从飞机上弹射而被卡塔尔抓获。 在伊朗媒体发表的致红十字国际委员会主席米里亚娜·斯波尔贾里奇的信中，他指责卡塔尔侵犯了“这些囚犯不可剥夺的权利，违反了所有国际法律和法规”。 信中还声称，三名飞行员不被允许会见或联系他们的家人。 卡塔尔外交事务发言人马吉德·穆罕默德·安萨里表示，“在飞行员侵犯卡塔尔领空后”与他们进行了联系，但尚未收到回应。 “我们根据国际法采取了必要措施来保卫我们的领土，”他在 X 的一份声明中补充道。 安萨里表示，卡塔尔搜救队“在搜寻飞行员遗体方面尽了最大努力”，并补充说，这个海湾国家已与伊朗联系“协调移交已找到的一名飞行员遗体”。 巴格扎德后来于周日告诉半官方的塔斯尼姆通讯社，卡塔尔应该允许伊朗实况调查小组进入该国调查发生的事情，并声称该小组已被拒绝入境数月。 安萨里表示，四月份邀请伊朗团队访问卡塔尔以审查其搜救行动结果的邀请已延长，但德黑兰尚未做出回应。

title.en: Hurricane Lala lashes Hawaii with strong winds and torrential rain
title.zh: 夏威夷为34年来首次飓风直接袭击做准备

summary.en: Hawaii is preparing for Hurricane Lala, which could be the first direct hit in 34 years, with a worst-case scenario predicting up to 25 inches (63cm) of rain on Big Island.
summary.zh: 夏威夷正为飓风拉拉可能带来的34年来首次直接袭击做准备，最坏情况下，大岛可能降下多达25英寸（63厘米）的雨量。

body.en:
Strong winds and torrential rain are lashing Hawaii after category one Hurricane Lala skirted Big Island on Saturday.

Hawaii Governor Josh Green said Lala got "closest to [Big Island's] South Point area", where a person died in weather-related a car accident.

Lala gained hurricane strength on Saturday after generating 80mph (130km/h) wind speeds, which have since peaked at 91mph. It could dump up to 25in (63cm) of rain and produce a 3ft storm surge.

Tens off thousands have been left without power and officials have warned people to prepare for "life-threatening" conditions, including floods and mudslides.

The storm is forecast to continue moving westward just south of Hawaii into Sunday morning.

A hurricane warning is in effect for Big Island, while Hawaii's seven other major islands - Maui, Molokai, Kahoolawe, Oahu, Lanai, Kauai and Niihau - are under tropical storm warnings.

The National Hurricane Center said that, as of 17:00 on Saturday local time (03:00 GMT on Sunday), Lala's eye wall was "brushing the southern portion of the Big Island".

"Damaging winds and heavy rain will persist across the Big Island throughout tonight and spread westwards across the smaller islands on Sunday," it said.

The hurricane did not make landfall, however, instead coming within 30 miles (48km) of South Point.

Green said many roads in Big Island had been affected, with 30 sites having already been visited by crews, and warned residents to brace for an "an incredible amount of water".

"Please be very safe... you do not want to be out on the roads," he said in a video update posted across his social media platforms.

Videos posted by Hawaii's Department of Transportation show roads flooded with fast-moving water and blocked with fallen trees.

At Ellison Onizuka Kona International - Big Island's largest airport - 40% of flights were grounded, according to tracker Flightaware. Some 80% of flights were called off at its other main airport, Hilo International.

The most dire forecasts from the National Weather Service (NWS) have been issued for areas within Big Island's south-east.

"Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues," the NWS said, adding that rivers and tributaries "may rapidly overflow their banks in multiple places".

More than 100,000 customers had lost electricity on Hawaii as of Saturday evening local time, according to tracker PowerOutage.

In Maui, some residents have also been left without water supply as of Saturday afternoon.

"Crews responded to the area but were unable to continue their assessment due to inclement weather and multiple downed trees," a county statement said, adding crews would return once it was safe.

title.en: Thousands displaced by deadly Indonesia earthquake as rescue efforts continue
title.zh: 救援人员搜寻印度尼西亚强震幸存者

summary.en: A powerful earthquake in Indonesia has destroyed hundreds of buildings and killed 47 people, with officials conducting a rapid assessment and rescuers searching for survivors.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚发生强烈地震，摧毁了数百座建筑物，造成47人死亡。目前，官员们正在进行快速评估，救援人员正在搜寻幸存者。

body.en:
Around 5,000 people have been displaced by a powerful earthquake in Indonesia that has caused at least 51 fatalities.

Rescuers continue to search for survivors of the shallow magnitude 7.7 quake, which struck the island of Flores shortly before 05:00 local time on Saturday (22:00 GMT on Friday).

Preliminary reports indicate more than 900 homes and hundreds of other buildings have been severely damaged by the tremor and 341 subsequent aftershocks, the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) said.

The full scale of the disaster is still being uncovered, with news of a second magnitude 6.9 earthquake elsewhere in Indonesia serving as a reminder of why this region is called the ring of fire.

The initial earthquake, which occurred just 15km below the surface, was the south-east Asian nation's deadliest since 2022, when hundreds of people were killed in West Java.

Tremors were reportedly felt by residents as far west as Bima, the BNPB said, but the Manggarai province was among the most affected.

Preliminary data shows 24 fatalities had been recorded there, while 17 deaths were recorded in East Manggarai province, three in Sikka province, and at least one in each of the Ngada, Ende and West Manggarai provinces.

A total of 3,356 people had been displaced in Sikka, with a further 2,078 evacuated in Manggarai, the agency said.

Thirty-six people were seriously injured in East Nusa Tenggara province, while 77 suffered minor injuries, Deputy Health Minister Benjamin Paulus Octavianus said.

It will take time to assess the full extent of the destruction in the region, which is remote and mountainous.

However, early reports indicate that, as well as more than 1,000 damaged homes, dozens of schools, healthcare facilities and government offices had also been severely damaged.

Ruteng Regional Hospital in Manggarai was among them. Images show operating theatre and clinic ceilings caved in, requiring patients to be treated in tents.

"We heard that medical assistance would be provided, but nothing has arrived yet," hospital spokesperson Rista Mari told BBC Indonesian. "We hope that assistance will arrive soon."

The BNPB said "meeting basic needs and providing logistics for evacuees has become one of the top priorities of the emergency response", adding it had dispatched tonnes of emergency supplies to Manggarai.

Video taken at the port in Maumere - the largest town in Flores - showed large chunks of concrete breaking off the terminal building onto passengers waiting to board an inter-island ferry. Some were thrown into the sea when the gangway to a ship collapsed.

Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena, governor of East Nusa Tenggara province, told a news conference that several of the victims had been killed in their sleep by collapsing rubble.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚的救援队一直在寻找星期六大地震的幸存者，这场地震造成至少 47 人死亡。 印度尼西亚气象和地球物理机构表示，在 05:00（格林威治标准时间周五 22:00）前不久，弗洛勒斯岛发生了 7.7 级地震，震源深度为 15 公里。 初步报告显示，数百座建筑物在地震和随后发生的数十次余震中严重受损。 然而，灾难的全面规模仍不清楚，印度尼西亚另一端发生第二次6.9级地震的消息提醒人们为什么他们称该地区为火环。 国家灾害管理局（BNPB）表示，据报道，远至西边的比马县和市的居民都感受到了周六强烈地震带来的震动，但芒加莱省是受影响最严重的省份之一。 初步数据显示，该地区已造成 24 人死亡，同时东芒加莱省有 17 人死亡，锡卡省有 3 人死亡，恩加达省、恩德省和西芒加莱省各至少有 1 人死亡。 BNPB 表示，目前已有 10,500 个包裹抵达基地，援助物资正在运往受影响地区。 该地区地处偏远，多山，需要时间来评估其破坏的全面程度。 然而，早期报告显示，150 多所房屋以及数十个教育机构、一些医疗设施、礼拜场所、办公室和其他一些公共设施遭到严重损坏。 在弗洛勒斯最大城镇毛梅雷的港口拍摄的视频显示，航站楼上有大块混凝土脱落，砸在等待登上岛际渡轮的乘客身上。当一艘船的舷梯倒塌时，一些人被扔进海里。 东努沙登加拉省省长伊曼纽尔·梅尔基亚德斯·拉卡·莱纳在新闻发布会上说，他们在睡梦中被倒塌的瓦砾炸死。 其他人，比如住在东努沙登加拉省锡卡海岸线附近塔利布拉村的阿诺德·韦利安托(Arnold Welianto)，都被从床上摇了起来。 他还告诉BBC，由于海水也退去了，许多人已经逃进山里。 虽然最初发布了海啸警报，导致约 2,000 人自行疏散，但在最初的震动大约三个小时后解除，当时没有检测到海平面明显上升。 然而，山体滑坡确实封锁了通往一些村庄的道路，但经验丰富的救援队全天不知疲倦地工作，以解救被困在废墟下的人们。 在如腾，医院外还搭建了临时医疗帐篷，用于救治地震灾民。 BNPB 持续建议人们保持冷静，远离沿海地区……

title.en: Troops from North Korea to boost Russia's Ukraine forces
title.zh: 朝鲜军队将增援俄罗斯在乌克兰的部队

summary.en: Intelligence agencies report that North Korea is preparing to send up to 50,000 troops to Russia to support its forces in Ukraine. However, military experts express skepticism that this deployment will significantly alter the trajectory of the conflict.
summary.zh: 情报机构报告称，朝鲜正准备向俄罗斯派遣多达5万名士兵，以增援其在乌克兰的部队。然而，军事专家们怀疑此举能否从根本上改变俄罗斯与乌克兰战争的进程。

body.en:
Intelligence agencies report that North Korea is preparing to send up to 50,000 troops to Russia. But military experts doubt that this will make a fundamental difference in the course of Russia's war with Ukraine.

In late 2024 , North Korea sent troops to help defend the Kursk region of Russia from Ukraine . International officials estimate that 14,000-15,000 North Korean troops were initially deployed to assist Russia in its war in Ukraine .. 

Now, Ukrainian and international intelligence agencies suspect that North Korea is planning to send an additional 30,000-50,000 troops to Russia . Ukrainian officials have also stated that North Korean ballistic missiles are being fired from Russia.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has raised concerns that North Korea's improved combat and weapons experience could pose a security threat to Ukraine, as well as the Asia-Pacific region.

Observers have had mixed responses to Zelenskyy's remarks. Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military and political expert at the Ukrainian Center for Security Studies, told DW that new troops from North Korea would likely be used to secure Russia's border territories. Aside from remaining in Kursk, North Korean soldiers could also help secure southwestern Vornezh.

"These forces could free up Russian occupational forces," Kovalenko said. "Russia would then be able to deploy around 15,000 troops to battles along front lines in Vovchansk, Kharkiv, Sumy or even Chernihiv."

Kovalenko does not expect North Korean troops to fight on Ukrainian territory. 

The Russian military analyst Ruslan Leviev agrees. "It's one thing to recapture Russian territory," he told DW, "and an entirely different thing to be present on internationally recognized Ukrainian territory, taking part in a war of aggression."

"Diplomatically speaking," he said, "those are two entirely different concepts."

Leviev said he had not seen concrete evidence of a noteworthy North Korean presence in Russia. He said Moscow had enough troops available without having to draw foreign soldiers into the fight. 

"If you look at the front line, you can see that Russia's forces have been fairly active since mid-July," Leviev said. "That's a clear sign they still have enough forces."

Estimates by the economist Janis Kluge, of the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), back this up. "While Russia's recruitment campaign has shown signs of strain this year, regional spending figures indicate that Russia is still recruiting around 1,000 contract soldiers each day,"  he recently wrote in a report .

title.en: Africa's low-key high-stakes Strait of Hormuz diplomacy
title.zh: 非洲在霍尔木兹海峡危机中的低调高风险外交

summary.en: African governments have maintained a discreet presence regarding the Strait of Hormuz crisis, despite their active, behind-the-scenes diplomatic engagement.
summary.zh: 在霍尔木兹海峡危机期间，非洲各国政府在国际舞台上保持低调。但这并不意味着它们没有在幕后积极参与处理这一问题。

body.en:
African governments have kept a low profile on the international stage during the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. But that doesn't mean they haven't been engaging with the issue behind the scenes.

One of the principal arteries of world trade has been chronically blocked for almost six months. Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has been reduced to a bare minimum since the first US-Israeli airstrikes on Iran at the end of February. Cargo ships have at times been fired on by Iranian forces; at others, threats from Tehran or Washington have been enough to bring shipping to a standstill.

So far, various rounds of talks , a joint memorandum and third-party deliberations about the creation of a maritime mission have not succeeded in stabilizing the situation. It remains to be seen whether a deal between Iran and Oman on establishing a shipping route through the strait will do so.

The war has prompted fossil fuel prices to soar all over the world, with inflation rising as a result. Despite its relative proximity to the Gulf region, some parts of Africa have experienced serious shortages because of the bottlenecks, with long lines of cars at gas stations that have run out of fuel. As many fertilizers are also sourced from the Gulf region, this year's harvests also threaten to be bad. African governments therefore have every reason to engage diplomatically in finding a permanent solution.

"I believe their long-term plan is still based on the assumption that the crisis in the Middle East may continue for some time," says Liesl Louw-Vaudran from the International Crisis Group , an NGO that works to prevent conflicts.

The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June, but Louw-Vaudran, an expert advisor working with the African Union, comments: "We don't see any evidence that there was some kind of optimism or revising of any economic planning after the MOU. I think everyone literally is just waiting to see how this is going to pan out in the next couple of months."

It's certainly the case that a low-key approach has dominated African diplomacy with regard to Hormuz in recent months. There have been numerous calls for negotiated solutions, praise for diplomatic initiatives and an emphasis on the rules-based order. Some African governments have also shown solidarity with the Arab Gulf states, which, as US allies, have come under fire from Iran.

The current African members of the UN Security Council — the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Somalia and Liberia — also backed a UN resolution adopted in March that strongly condemned Iranian attacks on the Gulf states.

However, it is apparent from their communications that African governments are trying to avoid apportioning blame — especially to the US president,...
body.zh: 霍尔木兹海峡危机期间，非洲各国政府在国际舞台上保持低调。但这并不意味着他们没有在幕后参与这个问题。 世界贸易的主要动脉之一已长期阻塞近六个月。自二月底美以首次对伊朗进行空袭以来，霍尔木兹海峡的海上交通已降至最低水平。货船有时会遭到伊朗军队的射击；在另一些人看来，来自德黑兰或华盛顿的威胁足以使航运陷入停滞。 迄今为止，关于设立海上使团的多轮会谈、联合备忘录和第三方审议尚未成功稳定局势。伊朗和阿曼之间关于建立穿过该海峡的航线的协议是否能实现这一目标还有待观察。 战争导致全球化石燃料价格飙升，通货膨胀率上升。尽管非洲部分地区距离海湾地区较近，但由于瓶颈，汽车在加油站排起长队，燃油耗尽，因此出现了严重的石油短缺。由于许多化肥也来自海湾地区，今年的收成也可能会不好。因此，非洲各国政府完全有理由通过外交手段寻求永久解决方案。 “我相信他们的长期计划仍然基于中东危机可能会持续一段时间的假设，”致力于预防冲突的非政府组织国际危机组织的莉斯·卢沃德兰 (Liesl Louw-Vaudran) 说。 美国和伊朗在六月签署了一份谅解备忘录，但与非洲联盟合作的专家顾问卢沃-沃德兰评论道：“我们没有看到任何证据表明谅解备忘录后出现了某种乐观情绪或对任何经济规划进行了修改。我认为每个人都在等待，看看未来几个月会如何发展。” 近几个月来，在霍尔木兹问题上，非洲外交确实以低调为主。人们多次呼吁通过谈判解决问题，赞扬外交举措，并强调基于规则的秩序。一些非洲国家政府也表现出了对阿拉伯海湾国家的声援，这些国家作为美国的盟友，受到了伊朗的攻击。 联合国安理会现任非洲成员国——刚果民主共和国、索马里和利比里亚——也支持联合国三月份通过的一项决议，该决议强烈谴责伊朗对海湾国家的袭击。 然而，从他们的沟通中可以明显看出，非洲各国政府正试图避免将责任归咎于美国总统……

reflection.en: In complex global situations, the pursuit of peace often requires quiet, persistent effort rather than public declarations. African nations' behind-the-scenes diplomacy in the Strait of Hormuz crisis reminds us that living peaceably with all, as far as it depends on us, is a continuous and often unseen endeavor. Such strategic engagement, even when low-key,...
reflection.zh: 在复杂的全球局势中，追求和平往往需要默默无闻、持之以恒的努力，而非公开声明。非洲国家在霍尔木兹海峡危机中进行的幕后外交提醒我们，尽力与众人和睦相处，是一项持续且常常不为人知的工作。这种战略性的参与，即使保持低调，对于促进稳定和防止局势升级也至关重要。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.zh: 黎巴嫩称以色列袭击造成至少11人死亡，敌对行动加剧

summary.en: Lebanon's leaders have condemned the strikes, which Israel's military said were in retaliation for an attack by Hezbollah.

body.en:
At least 11 people have been killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, the Lebanese health ministry said, some of the deadliest raids since deals in June eased hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah.

The Israeli military said it struck Hezbollah infrastructure overnight in what it describes as a security zone in southern Lebanon in response to actions against its soldiers there.

Iran-backed Hezbollah said in a statement that the attacks would be "met with what they deserve".

The framework leaves Israeli troops inside occupied southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed and the Lebanese army takes control, terms the group has rejected as surrender.

Lebanon's official National News Agency said seven people were killed when Israeli warplanes struck a house in the southern village of Ansar, while four others were killed in a strike on the village of Deir El Zahrani.

The seven people killed in Ansar included three children and two women, NNA said, adding that a total of 19 people were wounded in the attacks.

At least 4,300 people have been killed in Lebanon in the latest round of hostilities since 2 March.

NNA also reported other airstrikes across southern Lebanon, including on a strategic area north of the Litani River known as Ali al-Taher hill. One, targeting a valley next to Ansar, was the deepest strike into Lebanon in two months.

The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in a statement on X, accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire and attacking Israeli soldiers leading to three injuries.

"The IDF (Israel Defense Forces) responded by striking the Hezbollah terror headquarters which ordered the attack," the statement said. "Only later did the IDF learn that Hezbollah deliberately put civilians in that military compound."

The Israeli military said in a statement it killed Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a commander in Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force unit and others when it struck "a central headquarters of the Radwan Force unit", in Ansar.

"At the time of the strike, Hassan’s family was also present with him inside the military headquarters and, according to the claim, was harmed in the strike," the statement added, emphasising that the family was not the target of the strike.

"The martyrs of the Israeli raid on the village of Ansar are not 'military infrastructure' and the women and children killed in it are not military targets," Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said in a post on X.

title.en: Rescuers search desperately for survivors as Indonesian quake kills dozens of people
title.zh: 印度尼西亚地震造成数十人死亡，救援人员绝望搜寻幸存者

summary.en: Rescue teams are urgently working to reach the region closest to the epicenter of an Indonesian earthquake, where landslides have blocked roads and dozens of people have been killed.
summary.zh: 救援队正紧急赶往印度尼西亚地震震中附近地区，那里山体滑坡阻断了道路，已有数十人遇难。

body.en:
Rescuers have combed through debris for survivors after a powerful earthquake struck off Indonesia's eastern Flores island , killing 48 people and injuring dozens, according to disaster officials.

The national disaster management agency (BNPB) raised the death toll from 40 late on Saturday, and rescue official Fathur Rahman said 50 people were injured in the 7.7-magnitude quake.

Suharyanto, who leads the BNPB, said earlier that people were trapped in several buildings.

"These will be the initial targets of the disaster response teams," said Suharyanto, who like many Indonesians uses one name.

Nearly 160 houses, dozens of educational and health facilities and other public buildings were damaged when the earthquake struck the popular tourist island in Indonesia's east, the BNPB reported.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said preparations were underway to bring aid to some 2,000 people in temporary shelters.

The government sent 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the area, and European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the bloc's Copernicus Earth observation satellites.

"Europe stands ready to deploy Copernicus, our eyes in the sky, to support search and rescue efforts. Indonesia, we stand with you," she wrote on X.

"I have never felt an earthquake this big," Yulian Juita Ekalia, who lives in Ruteng city more than 100 kilometres west of the epicentre, told AFP by telephone hours after the tremor.

"It felt like we were on a trampoline; it was really scary," said the 37-year-old university lecturer, who was jolted awake at around 5.30am local time on Saturday.

"As I rushed to get outside, everything in the house fell down: the television, my son's trophies, the dish racks, suitcases on top of the wardrobes. When I got outside, my son and neighbours were already there, screaming in fear."

Rescue official Fathur told AFP the focus was on locating victims who may be buried under rubble, but rescue efforts have been complicated by landslides cutting off roads.

Residents in Nagekeo, an area close to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated early Saturday — a possible sign of an approaching tsunami , AFP journalists witnessed.

While a tsunami warning was lifted, authorities urged people not to return to damaged buildings for fear that aftershocks may bring them down.

Hundreds remained outside hours later as dozens of aftershocks shook the island, the strongest measured at a magnitude of 6.1.

title.en: Fujisawa is in his 70s and was jailed 15 times for shoplifting. He was desperate to go back

summary.en: As living costs rise, a growing number of elderly people in Japan are resorting to theft. For some, prison is not a deterrent, it’s the goal.

body.en:
Watch Dateline’s latest episode, Japan’s Shoplifting Pensioners, on 18 August at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand.

When Fujisawa walked out of prison for the fifteenth time, he had nowhere to go. No home, and no family waiting for him. After spending a total of 35 years behind bars for repeated shoplifting, remaining free meant uncertainty.

Fujisawa had been stealing tiny items of little use to him—lipstick, food, whatever he could grab quickly. Despite severe sentencing for repeat offenders in Japan, prison was never much of a deterrent. It meant returning to a community he was comfortable in.

"Once you’re in, you’re among friends, people who will accept who you are, whatever your background," he says.

Now in his seventies, Fujisawa has spent much of his adult life moving between prison and the outside world.

"I kept going in and out of prison," he says. I was only out in society for one or two years at a time."

While Fujisawa's story is extreme, he is part of a much broader problem in Japan.

Japan has one of the world's oldest populations, with more than a quarter of its citizens aged 65 or older. Its offenders are ageing too.

The proportion of elderly offenders has climbed despite overall crime rates falling dramatically. With people over 60 making up of more than a quarter of arrests in some parts of the country, many are accused of petty theft.

Volunteer probation officer Chiba has observed this shift. He says 20 to 30 per cent of his parolees are elderly.

"Being isolated and the rising cost of living, some old people don't receive enough pension. They run short on money, so they repeat crimes."

According to government data, around half of elderly people caught shoplifting live by themselves, with four in 10 saying they have no family or rarely speak to them.

The number of Japanese seniors living alone has dramatically increased over recent decades, leaving many to face old age with little financial or social support.

Elderly offenders also have some of Japan's highest rates of reoffending. Nearly one in five prisoners over 60 returns to prison within two years of being released.

Last year, the government amended the Penal Code, abolishing mandatory prison labour and introducing rehabilitation programs to give prisoners skills to help them cope with life on the outside.

But former prisoners coming back to the outside still face social stigma. Many struggle to find work and secure housing.

"Historically in Japan, our attitudes towards former prisoners and how we treat them has not been good," Chiba says .

title.en: Fiji, Israel and the Lost Tribe at the ends of the Earth
title.zh: 斐济与以色列深厚渊源背后的惊人故事

summary.en: Fiji's unexpected and strong relationship with Israel is rooted in a unique national origin story that has influenced both the island nation's local faith practices and its international diplomatic approach.
summary.zh: 斐济与以色列之间出人意料的紧密关系，植根于一个独特的国家起源故事，这个故事影响了斐济的乡村信仰实践及其国际外交政策。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

Long ago, the story goes, a great double-hulled canoe called the Kaunitoni came from the west, carrying the first ancestral chiefs of the iTaukei (indigenous Fijians). At its head, in one version of the tradition, stood their leader, Lutunasobasoba.

The voyagers had come a seemingly impossible distance: from Thebes in ancient Egypt — earlier still, some say, from a place farther west, via Israel — down the Nile to Lake Tanganyika, across the Indian Ocean, and finally to Vuda, on the western coast of Viti Levu, Fiji's largest island.

In some tellings, it carried the written record of the people's laws and genealogies — lost, like the canoe's other cargo, somewhere in the churning sea.

For most of the past century, this has been one of the best-known versions of Fiji's national origin story. The mission schools taught it; so did the primary schools. Radio carried it further still, until it became part of the way generations of Fijians understood their ancestry.

Only, much of it was invented in the 1890s — set down for the first time in a newspaper.

The colonial government's Fijian-language paper, Na Mata, ran a competition at the time, inviting readers across the archipelago to send in the definitive account of where the Fijian people had come from, with the best to be printed.

The winning entry ran over 17 instalments, centring on a forgotten tribe. Within a few decades it had acquired the weight of history.

Behind the claimed migration sits a larger conviction, still widely held in some iTaukei communities and church groups: that Fijians descend from a Lost Tribe of Israel — one of 10 the Hebrew Bible describes as carried into exile and never heard from again.

The belief has no support in mainstream science or archaeology. Yet it has helped foster a distinctive affinity with Israel.

The particulars shift from place to place. On Mana Island, in the Yasawa group off western Viti Levu, the Ark of the Covenant — the gold-covered chest that, in the Book of Exodus, held the Ten Commandments — is said to lie buried.

In a village in Ba, in Viti Levu's north-west, an elder once pointed to a rock and told Reverend Marika Baleidelabaci, a Fijian historian and Methodist minister, that Jesus had been born exactly there.

In the Navosa highlands, markings cut into a cave wall are read by some as ancient Hebrew — an interpretation, Baleidelabaci says, that came back with Fijian soldiers who had served in the Middle East and recognised the shapes.

title.en: Lebanon says 11 killed in Israeli airstrikes
title.zh: 黎巴嫩称以色列空袭造成11人死亡

summary.en: Lebanon's prime minister reported that 11 people were killed in Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanese villages, accusing Israel of targeting civilians in their homes. Israel stated its strikes were aimed at Hezbollah infrastructure.
summary.zh: 黎巴嫩总理报告称，以色列对黎巴嫩南部村庄的空袭造成11人死亡，并指责以色列袭击了平民住宅。以色列则表示其袭击目标是真主党的基础设施。

body.en:
Lebanon's prime minister denounced the attacks on villages in southern Lebanon for targeting civilians in their homes. Israel said it was firing on Hezbollah infrastructure.

At least 11 people were killed when Israel launched fresh airstrikes in southern Lebanon  on Saturday, the deadliest since the Israel-Hezbollah truce nearly two months ago.

The attacks were met with defiance by the Iran-backed Hezbollah , which demanded an end to "humiliating" peace negotiations with Israel .

The Lebanese Health Ministry said one of the strikes, on the edge of the village of Ansar, killed seven people and wounded two.

The strike, which happened at dawn, hit a house and destroyed it, according to NNA, the Lebanese state news agency.

Germany's DPA news agency cited residents as saying the property served as a base for Hezbollah.

The second strike hit the village of Deir al-Zahrani, killing four and wounding 17.

NNA reported other strikes around the strategic Ali Taher hill, which overlooks parts of the southern city of Nabatiyeh and key roads to it.

The Israeli military confirmed hitting Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, saying it was retaliation for an attack by the militia on Israeli forces.

Later Saturday, Hezbollah hit back at the latest strikes, saying they would be met with an "appropriate" response.

Israel "must clearly understand that its attacks, violations and attempts to impose a fait accompli cannot continue, and will be met with an appropriate response", the Iran-backed group said in a statement.

Hezbollah warned Lebanese authorities against continuing its "humiliating" negotiations with Israel, which would provide "the enemy with free concessions."

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam denounced the strikes, calling on Israel to "halt this escalation."

"The seven martyrs of the Israeli airstrike on the town of Ansar are not military infrastructure and the children and women killed were not military targets,” he wrote on X.

The Israel–Hezbollah war reignited in early March around the start of the  Iran war , when Hezbollah launched attacks on northern Israel to avenge the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

It rapidly became a full-scale conflict that involved Israeli ground operations in southern Lebanon, mass evacuations of residents and the deaths of over 4,300 people.

Israel claims to have established the so-called security zone in southern Lebanon to prevent Hezbollah attacks on northern Israel. 

According to Lebanese media, the Israeli-controlled area covers approximately 620 square kilometres, or about 6% of the country's total area.

body.zh: 黎巴嫩总理谴责黎巴嫩南部村庄针对平民家中的袭击。以色列称其正在向真主党基础设施​​开火。 周六，以色列对黎巴嫩南部发动新的空袭，造成至少 11 人死亡，这是近两个月前以色列与真主党休战以来最严重的一次空袭。 这些袭击遭到伊朗支持的真主党的反抗，真主党要求结束与以色列的“羞辱性”和平谈判。 黎巴嫩卫生部表示，其中一次袭击发生在安萨尔村边缘，造成七人死亡、两人受伤。 据黎巴嫩国家通讯社 NNA 报道，这次袭击发生在黎明，击中了一所房屋并将其摧毁。 德国德新社援引居民的话说，该房产是真主党的基地。 第二次袭击袭击了代尔扎赫拉尼 (Deir al-Zahrani) 村，造成 4 人死亡、17 人受伤。 NNA 报道了战略要地阿里塔赫山周围发生的其他袭击事件，该山俯瞰着南部城市纳巴提耶的部分地区及其主要道路。 以色列军方证实袭击了黎巴嫩南部真主党的基础设施，称这是对民兵袭击以色列军队的报复。 周六晚些时候，真主党对最近的袭击进行了反击，称他们将得到“适当”的回应。 伊朗支持的组织在一份声明中表示，以色列“必须清楚地认识到，其袭击、侵犯行为和强加既成事实的企图不能继续下去，并将得到适当的回应”。 真主党警告黎巴嫩当局不要继续与以色列进行“羞辱性”谈判，这将为“敌人提供自由的让步”。 黎巴嫩总理纳瓦夫·萨拉姆谴责了这次袭击，呼吁以色列“停止升级”。 “以色列对安萨尔镇空袭的七名烈士不是军事基础设施，被杀的儿童和妇女也不是军事目标，”他在 X 上写道。 以色列与真主党的战争在 3 月初伊朗战争爆发前后重新燃起，当时真主党对以色列北部发动袭击，为伊朗最高领袖阿亚图拉·阿里·哈梅内伊被杀报仇。 这场冲突迅速演变成一场全面冲突，涉及以色列在黎巴嫩南部的地面行动、居民大规模疏散以及 4,300 多人死亡。 以色列声称在黎巴嫩南部建立了所谓的安全区，以防止真主党袭击以色列北部。 据黎巴嫩媒体报道，以色列控制区面积约620平方公里，约占该国总面积的6%。 该协议制定了以色列军队从黎巴嫩南部撤军的计划......

reflection.en: The tragic loss of civilian lives in conflict reminds us of the urgent need to speak for those who are vulnerable and silenced. Yahweh calls us to advocate for the rights of the destitute and to ensure justice for all who cannot defend themselves. In times of violence, our compassion must extend to those caught in the crossfire.
reflection.zh: 冲突中平民生命的悲惨逝去提醒我们，迫切需要为那些脆弱无声的人发声。雅伟呼召我们为贫困者的权利仗义执言，并确保所有无法自卫的人都能获得公义。在暴力时期，我们的怜悯必须延伸到那些身陷战火的人。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: China Desk
title.zh: 中国观察

strap.en: Policy signals, social change, and national developments inside China.
strap.zh: 聚焦中国内部政策走向、社会变化与国家动态。

title.en: How to buy a ‘mega-dinghy’: the perilous new model of Channel crossing
title.zh: 如何购买“巨型橡皮艇”：危险的英吉利海峡偷渡新模式

summary.en: The Guardian China reports on the alarming trend of large dinghies, capable of carrying hundreds, being used for perilous Channel crossings. The article investigates the supply chain for these vessels, noting that large orders are readily fulfilled by manufacturers.
summary.zh: 《卫报》中国版报道称，载有数百人的大型充气艇被用于危险的英吉利海峡偷渡，这一趋势令人担忧。文章调查了这些大型船只的来源，指出制造商可以轻松满足大批量订单。

body.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. Additional reporting by Lyndon Li Continue reading...
body.zh: 载有数百人的船只是一个明显且令人震惊的趋势。但这么大的船只从哪里来呢？他们表示，只要订单超过 20 艘，提供一艘在西欧波涛汹涌的海域使用的大型小艇就不成问题。这家中国公司的销售经理甚至还为一位冒充潜在客户的卫报卧底记者准备了一份在线手册供其细读。他们的生产能力为每月 500 艘船，是的，有可能以合适的价格获得更大的船。他们可以以每艘 1,678 美元（1,238 英镑）的价格制造一艘七米甚至八米长的军用小艇，不带发动机，但这将缺乏 CE 认证，这是表明产品符合欧盟健康和安全要求的强制性标志。林登·李的补充报道继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report on the supply of vessels for perilous journeys reminds us of the vulnerable individuals seeking safety and new beginnings. Yahweh calls us to recognize His presence in those who are marginalized and in desperate need. Our compassion for 'the least of these' reflects our love for Him.
reflection.zh: 这篇关于用于危险旅程的船只供应的报道，提醒我们那些寻求安全和新生活的弱势个体。雅伟呼召我们要在那些被边缘化和极度需要的人身上认出祂的存在。我们对“这些最小的弟兄”的怜悯，反映了我们对祂的爱。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: The Fauci hearing was painful to watch. But we need answers on Covid-19’s origin| David Relman
title.zh: 福奇听证会令人痛苦，但我们需要新冠病毒起源的答案 | 大卫·雷尔曼

summary.en: Despite recent congressional hearings, understanding the origin of Covid-19 remains elusive, with a microbiologist observing a deterioration in public discourse surrounding the issue.
summary.zh: 尽管近期国会举行了听证会，但了解新冠病毒的起源仍然困难重重，一位微生物学家指出，围绕这一问题的公共讨论正在恶化。

body.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19 origins. It has been especially difficult for me to read the comments of Anthony Fauci about the origins debate in his now-public diary . And it has been painful to watch the televised spectacle hosted by the US senator Rand Paul on 29 July involving a hostile interrogation of Fauci. Despite many early pleas, including my own , for a dispassionate, objective assessment of what we know, don’t know and need to know about Covid-19 origins, we seem to be even further from this goal now than we have ever been – plagued by politicization, polarization and illogical thinking. David Relman is a professor of medicine and microbiology at Stanford University. He was an inaugural member of the US National Science Advisory Board for Biosecurity and president of the Infectious Diseases Society of America Continue reading...
body.zh: 尽管最近在国会举行了听证会，但我们似乎距离了解 Covid-19 起源的目标比以往任何时候都更远。作为一名微生物学家和传染病临床医生，很难看到最近公众关于 Covid-19 起源的讨论的转移。对我来说，阅读安东尼·福奇在他现已公开的日记中关于起源争论的评论尤其困难。 7 月 29 日美国参议员兰德·保罗主持的电视节目对福奇进行敌意审讯，令人感到痛苦。尽管包括我自己在内的许多人早期呼吁对我们所知道、不知道和需要了解的 Covid-19 起源进行冷静、客观的评估，但我们现在似乎比以往任何时候都离这个目标更远——受到政治化、两极分化和不合逻辑思维的困扰。大卫·雷尔曼是斯坦福大学医学和微生物学教授。他是美国国家生物安全科学咨询委员会的首任成员和美国传染病学会主席继续阅读...

reflection.en: The struggle to understand complex issues like the origin of Covid-19, especially amidst contentious public discourse, reminds us of the wisdom in seeking thorough examination. Proverbs 18:17 suggests that true understanding emerges only after hearing all sides and carefully scrutinizing every claim. This calls for patience and a commitment to truth beyond...
reflection.zh: 在围绕新冠病毒起源等复杂问题展开的激烈公共讨论中，我们努力寻求理解，这提醒我们彻底审查的重要性。箴言18:17指出，真正的理解只有在听取各方意见并仔细审查每项主张之后才能浮现。这要求我们超越初步印象，以耐心和对真理的承诺，从而走向更清晰的道路。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: ‘TikTok wouldn’t open at all’: Taiwan simulates an internet blackout, with an eye on China threat
title.zh: “抖音完全打不开”：台湾模拟互联网中断，以应对中国威胁

summary.en: Taiwan conducted its first internet blackout simulation, prompted by concerns over the security of its undersea cables, which are vital for its digital connectivity. During the exercise in Taipei, air raid sirens sounded, mobile alerts pinged, and police directed people off the streets.
summary.zh: 台湾周四首次进行互联网中断模拟演习，原因是担心作为其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全。在台北的演习中，防空警报响起，手机警报提示音不断，警察引导人们离开街道。

body.en: Taiwan practised cutting off internet for the first time amid concerns about the safety of the undersea cables that form its ‘digital lifeline’ In Taipei, the streets swiftly empty as air raid sirens ring out and alerts ping on mobile phones. Police officers usher any stragglers into shelters, leaving the capital suddenly deserted. In cities across Taiwan, these kinds of drills are a fact of life every year , amid the growing threat posed by China across the strait, but this time there is something different. Continue reading...
body.zh: 由于担心构成其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全性，台湾周四首次练习切断互联网。在台北，随着空袭警报的响起和手机上的警报声，街道迅速空无一人。警察把掉队的人带进避难所，首都突然变得空无一人。在台湾各城市，随着海峡两岸中国构成的威胁日益加剧，此类演习每年都是家常便饭，但这次有所不同。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Taiwan's simulation of an internet blackout highlights the deep anxieties nations face regarding critical infrastructure and potential threats. In moments of such vulnerability and preparation, the ancient promise of Yahweh reminds us not to fear or be dismayed, for divine presence offers strength and help. This spiritual anchor can guide communities as...
reflection.zh: 台湾模拟互联网中断，凸显了各国在关键基础设施和潜在威胁面前的深层焦虑。在面对这种脆弱和准备的时刻，雅伟的古老应许提醒我们不要惧怕，也不要惊惶，因为神圣的同在提供力量和帮助。这个属灵的锚点可以指引社群应对复杂的挑战并建立韧性。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: The west turns a blind eye to Xi Jinping’s repressive regime in China | Letters
title.zh: 西方国家对习近平在中国的压制性政权视而不见 | 来信

summary.en: Jennifer Hubbard and other letter writers express concern that Western nations are ignoring China's repressive regime, particularly its 'ethnic unity' law used to suppress minorities. They argue that meaningful international diplomacy is urgently needed to address these human rights issues.
summary.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德及其他来信者表示，西方国家对中国压制性政权，特别是其用于压制少数民族的“民族团结”法视而不见。他们认为，急需有意义的国际外交来解决这些人权问题。

body.en: Meaningful diplomacy on an international level is well overdue, writes Jennifer Hubbard . Plus letters from Geoffrey Dixon and Jane Renton In his article on China’s latest tool for suppression of minorities, the “ethnic unity” law, Simon Tisdall seems to take it as read that western governments will continue to pay lip service to notions of human rights in China while pursuing short-term economic goals, ultimately destructive to their own productivity ( President Xi never wastes a good crisis. As Iran, Ukraine and Palestine distract the world, he tightens his grip, 8 August ). This has been the pattern since June 1989, the Tiananmen Square massacre. His faint hope that the young urban Chinese might overturn Xi’s regime is a judgment on the failure of western governments to show any foresight, integrity, effective diplomacy, joined-up thinking or action. They rely on the self-sacrifice of individuals such as Jimmy Lai , Lobga Rangzen and countless – often to us nameless – individuals who put their lives on the line while we wring our hands and weep crocodile tears. Continue reading...
body.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德写道，早就应该在国际层面开展有意义的外交。再加上杰弗里·迪克森和简·伦顿的来信。西蒙·蒂斯达尔在其关于中国镇压少数民族的最新工具“民族团结”法的文章中似乎认为，西方政府将继续对中国的人权观念口头上说好，同时追求短期经济目标，最终损害他们自己的生产力（习主席从来不会浪费一场好的危机。随着伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦分散了世界的注意力，他加强了控制，8月8日）。这就是1989年6月天安门广场屠杀以来的模式。他对中国城市年轻人可能推翻习近平政权的微弱希望是对西方政府未能表现出任何远见、正直、有效外交、联合思维或行动的判断。他们依赖于黎智英（Jimmy Lai）、洛布加·让赞（Lobga Rangzen）等个人的自我牺牲，以及无数（通常对我们来说无名）个人的自我牺牲，他们冒着生命危险，而我们则绞尽脑汁，流下鳄鱼的眼泪。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for international diplomacy to address the suppression of minorities echoes the biblical mandate to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves. In a world where powerful voices can overshadow the vulnerable, Yahweh reminds us of our responsibility to advocate for justice and the rights of the destitute. May we seek wisdom and courage to uphold...
reflection.zh: 呼吁国际外交以解决少数民族受压迫的问题，与圣经中为不能为自己说话之人发声的命令不谋而合。在一个强大声音可能掩盖弱势群体的世界里，雅伟提醒我们有责任倡导正义和维护贫困者的权利。愿我们寻求智慧和勇气，维护所有人的尊严，特别是那些声音被压制的人。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
title.zh: 台湾称遭受“异常”人工智能辅助网络攻击

summary.en: Taiwan reported detecting "abnormal" AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies last month, originating from overseas. These attacks represent a new kind of threat, with suspected links to China-based hackers.
summary.zh: 台湾报告称，上个月侦测到来自海外、由人工智能辅助的“异常”网络攻击，目标是政府机构。这些攻击代表了一种新型威胁，据称与中国相关黑客有关。

body.en: Taiwan’s statement comes a day after reports that suspected China-linked hackers had carried out a first-of-a-kind breach Taiwan says it detected AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies that came from overseas last month, a new kind of threat that has been reported as “first-of-a-kind breach”. The Ministry of Digital Affairs (MDA) said its cybersecurity monitoring units ‌detected the “abnormal attack” targeting government agencies, which began on 20 July. The National Institute of Cyber Security issued a series of warning alerts while it investigated. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾发表声明的前一天，有报道称疑似与中国有关的黑客实施了史无前例的违规行为。台湾表示，上个月检测到来自海外的针对政府机构的人工智能辅助网络攻击，这是一种新的威胁，被报道为“史无前例的违规行为”。数字事务部 (MDA) 表示，其网络安全监控单位检测到 7 月 20 日开始的针对政府机构的“异常攻击”。美国国家网络安全研究所在调查过程中发布了一系列警告。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The emergence of AI-assisted cyber-attacks highlights the constant need for vigilance in a rapidly changing world. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that wisdom lies in foreseeing danger and taking appropriate refuge. As technology evolves, so must our discernment and protective measures, trusting Yahweh for guidance.
reflection.zh: 人工智能辅助的网络攻击的出现，凸显了在快速变化的世界中保持警惕的持续必要性。箴言27:12提醒我们，智慧在于预见危险并采取适当的避难措施。随着科技发展，我们的洞察力和保护措施也必须随之进步，信靠雅伟的指引。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: With Hollywood struggling in China, can the Odyssey draw a crowd?
title.zh: 好莱坞在中国市场举步维艰，《奥德赛》能否吸引观众？

summary.en: Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster, "The Odyssey" (likely Oppenheimer), is set for release across China's Imax screens. This comes at a time when Western films generally face difficulties in the Chinese market, and the film itself has reportedly overcome significant opposition.
summary.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》（很可能是《奥本海默》）将在中国各地的IMAX影院上映。目前西方电影在中国市场普遍举步维艰，而这部影片据报道也克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击。

body.en: Christopher Nolan’s epic will be released on Friday across most of the country’s 800 Imax screens, at a time when western films have been struggling The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster juggernaut, has overcome an onslaught of attacks from the world’s richest man and stared down criticism from a classicist who translated the poem , to become one of the year’s most celebrated and highest-grossing films. But this week, the film faces one of its biggest challenges yet. Continue reading...
body.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的这部史诗巨制将于周五在全国 800 块 Imax 银幕上上映，当时西方电影一直在苦苦挣扎，克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击，也顶住了翻译这首诗的古典学家的批评，成为今年最著名和票房最高的电影之一。但本周，这部电影面临着迄今为止最大的挑战之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Launching any major endeavor, like a film in a challenging market, requires immense effort and hope for success. Proverbs 16:3 reminds us to commit our work to Yahweh, trusting that He will establish our plans. Even when facing significant headwinds, we can find peace in knowing that our diligent efforts are seen and can be blessed.
reflection.zh: 在充满挑战的市场中推出一部电影这样的大型项目，需要付出巨大的努力并寄予成功的希望。箴言16:3提醒我们，要将我们的工作交托给雅伟，相信他会成就我们的计划。即使面对重重阻力，我们也能在知道自己的辛勤努力被看见并蒙福时找到平安。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Zhu Rongji obituary
title.zh: 朱镕基讣告

summary.en: Zhu Rongji, the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China, has passed away at 97. He was widely recognized as an economic reformer who famously declared China 'the factory of the world' and was regarded as one of the country's most effective administrators.
summary.zh: 中华人民共和国第五任总理朱镕基逝世，享年97岁。他被广泛认为是经济改革家，曾宣布中国成为‘世界工厂’，并被视为该国最有效的管理者之一。

body.en: Premier of the People’s Republic of China regarded as an economic reformer who declared that the country had become ‘the factory of the world’ Zhu Rongji, who has died aged 97, was the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China and one of its most effective administrators and economic reformers following its foundation in 1949. In 1991, Zhu was summoned to Beijing, in the footsteps of the then president and party secretary Jiang Zemin , and in the aftermath of the 1989 uprisings in Beijing and the collapse of the Soviet Union. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The passing of a leader like Zhu Rongji marks the end of a significant chapter, reflecting a life dedicated to public service and economic reform. His legacy reminds us that every life is a race run, with efforts and impacts that shape the world around us. Yahweh invites us to consider how we too might finish our own race with integrity and purpose.
reflection.zh: 朱镕基这样一位领导人的逝世，标志着一个重要篇章的结束，反映了他一生致力于公共服务和经济改革。他的遗产提醒我们，每个人的一生都是一场赛跑，其努力和影响塑造着我们周围的世界。雅伟邀请我们思考，我们又将如何以正直和目标跑完自己的赛程。

verse.textEn: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
verse.textZh: 那美好的仗我已经打过了，当跑的路我已经跑尽了，所信的道我已经守住了。

title.en: 'Not where the problems are': Working holiday visa slowdown divides parties
title.zh: “问题不在那里”：打工度假签证放缓引发党派分歧

summary.en: Working holidaymakers fill a labour shortage doing jobs like fruit picking, waiting tables and guiding tours in regional areas.

body.en:
The federal government has confirmed it will slow the processing of working holiday visa applications as pressure mounts to reduce net migration numbers. 

Nine newspapers first reported on Saturday that the federal government had paused applications for working holiday visas from 24 countries.

But Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke confirmed on Sunday that working holiday visas were still being processed, but they were being handled "more slowly than they were previously".

However, when asked about the impact of fewer backpackers on the agriculture sector, he pointed to a Pacific workers' scheme as the primary visa for temporary staff.

"One of the things that happened when we started to improve worker protections on (the Pacific scheme) was ... some of the worst operators said, "if we've got to have better standards for (those) workers, we'll just switch to backpackers".

Working holiday visas — often called "backpacker visas" — allow travellers to extend their stay in Australia by undertaking work that addresses labour shortages in Australia — often fruit picking, farm work, mining, or tourism work in regional and remote areas.

The number of working holiday visa holders in Australia passed 210,000 in June 2025, outpacing pre-COVID figures by around 100,000.

The move comes as pressure builds on the Albanese government to bring down net overseas migration, with other parties carving out their migration policy.

Migration experts have warned of the dangers of political parties attempting to blame migrants for a lack of homes , arguing that migrant workforces will be essential to building the required housing stock

Net overseas migration — a measure covering visitors, family and partner visas, working holidaymakers, skilled migration, and humanitarian intake, alongside returning Australians — fell slightly to 301,000 in 2025, down from 306,000 the year before, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

Labor's long-term target is 225,000 a year over the next three years, though Burke said on Sunday the party's migration policy was still being worked through and needed to go through a full cabinet process.

None of the major parties has yet specified which visa categories they'd cut to hit their targets — though the Coalition has said intake should be tied to housing competitions rather than a fixed annual figure.

title.en: Government admits NDIS reforms will impact families, downplays fears over state readiness
title.zh: 政府承认国家残疾保险计划改革将影响家庭，淡化对各州准备情况的担忧

summary.en: The federal disability minister has defended proposed changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), acknowledging that the reforms will affect families. The minister also indicated that further amendments are planned to combat fraud and secure parliamentary approval.
summary.zh: 联邦残疾事务部长为国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）的改革措施进行了辩护，承认这些改革将影响到家庭。部长还表示，将进一步修订以打击欺诈行为并争取议会支持。

body.en:
Labor has downplayed concerns that state-based disability supports won't be ready when needed, as the government pushes contentious NDIS reforms targeting fraud and spending through parliament.

A government-led Senate inquiry on Friday recommended National Disability Insurance Scheme changes should be passed with no substantial alterations.

The overhaul would cut a targeted $37.8 billion from the NDIS over four years and remove 160,000 participants by tightening eligibility requirements.

NDIS Minister Jenny McAllister said a deal between the government and the coalition to pass the changes was getting close.

"We're really hopeful and I'd go as far as saying confident that we can reach an agreement," she told ABC's Insiders program on Sunday.

Opposition health spokeswoman Anne Ruston called for a strengthened fraud and corruption response within the disability insurance agency in the inquiry report.

Senator McAllister said the government was still considering evidence brought forward during the inquiry process and flagged fraud as an area to work through with the coalition.

But concerns about the changes remain among advocates — and from at least one state.

In a joint statement, 12 disability advocacy organisations said the reforms should not pass parliament in their current form.

"It must guarantee that people are not diverted from, or lose, NDIS supports unless alternative supports are funded, operational, accessible and available in practice."

Queensland has resisted signing up to the Thriving Kids program, a major plank in federal plans to cut costs from the NDIS.

Under the program, which is due to be rolled out from October, some children aged eight and under with autism or developmental delays would be shifted onto state supports.

Queensland Disability Minister Amanda Camm has refused to back the agreement, labelling the change a cost-shifting exercise that lacked detail.

Despite the conflict, Labor remained confident people with a disability would not be left without the support they needed.

"We don't need to contemplate delay at this point, because we are working with the states and territories toward that January 1 deadline."

Labor's NDIS plan would lead to average funding being cut by about $5000 a year for participants.

"It is a reduction and we don't deny that it will have impacts on people with disability and their families," Senator McAllister said.

She again dismissed calls to introduce an NDIS inspector-general, saying it would risk adding another layer of bureaucracy.

body.en:
Pauline Hanson has doubled down on notorious decades-old comments criticising Sydney's Mardi Gras, saying she thinks people should keep their sexuality "behind closed doors".

The comments come only days after a colleague declared One Nation "one of the gayest parties in Australia".

In an infamous 1996 interview with 60 Minutes, the right-wing party's leader responded "I don't like it" while offering her thoughts on the annual LGBTIQ+ festival.

"I don't like it because it's promoting something ... that is not natural," she said at the time.

Her "I don't like it" comment was co-opted by drag queen Pauline Pantsdown in 1998 and remixed into a parody dance song, which made it into the Triple J Hottest 100 list of that year.

"I still don't like the gay Mardi Gras, but that's my opinion," she told News24 on Sunday.

"I think your own, personal sexuality should be kept ... behind closed doors. It's no one's business to do it out there with the gay Mardi Gras anywhere.

"I know it brings a lot of tourists to the country. I know it brings a lot of money. I know all this, but that’s my personal opinion. But anyway, good luck to them that they want to do that."

Her comments follow revelations One Nation's candidate for Western Australia's upper house at the 2025 election, Parminder Singh, made several anti-gay comments in a video on social media.

Mr Singh, who was third on One Nation's upper house ticket at the state election, has since been removed from the party's website, after the video became public.

During the week, One Nation MP Barnaby distanced the party from its former candidate's views, describing it as "one of the gayest parties in Australia".

Senator Hanson also rejected Ms Singh's comments, saying she never heard similar views from him when he was a candidate.

The firebrand politician also defended her inability to name the leaders of crucial allies and regional powers when questioned about her foreign policy credentials as a would-be prime minister.

In an earlier interview with News24, the One Nation leader said diplomacy with Australia's neighbours would pose "no problem", despite her notoriously using her maiden speech in 1996 to declare the nation was "in danger of being swamped by Asians".

Asked if she could name the president of Indonesia or the prime minister of Japan, two major regional powers and key Australian trading partners, Senator Hanson said she couldn't.

summary.en: The federal and New South Wales governments have agreed on a gun buyback scheme for the state, initiated after the 2025 Bondi shooting massacre.

body.en:
An agreement has been struck on a major federal-state gun buyback following the Bondi shooting massacre, with the Commonwealth and New South Wales governments to evenly share the cost of the scheme.

NSW tightened its laws in the days following the December 2025 attack by introducing gun ownership limits, reclassifying some types of weapons, boosting background checks and reducing firearms licences from five years to two.

The buyback is now considered the next step in the reforms — and is informed by the interim recommendations of the anti-Semitism royal commission.

"We must do everything we can to make sure the anti-Semitic terrorist attack in Bondi doesn't happen again," Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Sunday.

But the hope for a truly national scheme is far from certain. NSW is so far the only state to come aboard, with several states rejecting joining outright — and it also faces mounting opposition from political parties, including One Nation.

The first phase of the scheme, set to begin on 2 November 2026, will see $1,000 paid to people who hand in their revolvers, $850 for semi-automatic handguns, $850 for double-barrel shotguns and $650 for those with a single barrel.

Compensation will be paid for firearms beyond the new ownership limits and for newly reclassified firearms, along with a flat fee for associated ammunition.

The scheme will also provide financial assistance for businesses and industry to adjust to the reforms.

The Commonwealth will contribute 50 per cent for administration costs and fully fund the destruction of surrendered weapons. 

A fixed price schedule will apply for individual licence holders beyond the new legal limit to return their firearms in exchange for compensation.

Eligible businesses and dealers will be offered up to $25,000 in grants and one-off licence fee relief worth $500 over two years per dealer.

Early 2027 will see a pathway to compensation, for a fee, for eligible higher-value firearms with an indicative market value above $3,000 and capped at $10,000 per firearm.

It's estimated up to 274,000 registered firearms or about 24 per cent of the total number of registered guns in NSW — and some 50,000 licence holders — are affected by the new limits on ownership. 

The buyback scheme has been branded a national one — though NSW is the only state participating right now.

Queensland and Victoria have rejected the scheme outright, while the NT was firm that it would not fund a buyback.

title.en: Property investors are retreating — so why isn't this a win for first-home buyers?
title.zh: 投资者已退出房地产市场。但你会受益吗？

summary.en: New data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics indicates an 8.6 per cent drop in investor loans during the June quarter, raising questions about the long-term presence of investors in the housing market.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚统计局的最新数据显示，6月份投资者贷款数量下降了8.6%，这引发了关于投资者是否会永久退出房地产市场的问题。

body.en:
Investors are shying away from the housing market — but experts say it might not be the win the government says it is.

New Australian Bureau of Statistics data on loans show investors have pulled back sharply from the housing market in the June quarter.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said on Friday the lending figures were an "encouraging sign" that Labor's changes to negative gearing and the capital gains discount were working as intended and the market was "shifting in favour of first-home buyers" — even before the changes have officially taken effect.

But experts said the retreat hasn't necessarily translated into the wave of first-home buyers the federal government's property tax changes were designed to generate.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The number of investor loans fell 8.6 per cent in the June quarter, while first-home buyer loans fell a comparatively lower 2.9 per cent, according to ABS data released on Friday.

Independent property researcher Cameron Kusher said ABS' latest lending data was not surprising and reflected a typical knee-jerk reaction to policy changes.

“Across both the number and the value, the biggest falls in lending over the quarter were for investors, which is not really a surprise when you consider the tax changes that have happened,” he said.

The pullback lines up with what major banks have been reporting in their own lending figures, with CBA and NAB both reporting a 15 per cent drop in mortgage applications last quarter, while Westpac saw a 20 per cent drop.

The tax changes were announced in the May budget but aren't set to formally take effect until 1 July 2027. So, this quarter's fall was a reaction to the announcement itself, not the policy in action.

"We may actually see a larger fall when we get to the next quarter, when we see the full impact of a whole quarter of these changes," he said.

Both Kusher and Real Estate Group's economist Luc Redman say investors have not retreated entirely, rather they have changed strategy.

They are still keen on residential property but the type of property they’re chasing has shifted. They are now eyeing properties that have strong rental growth, or yield.

"Early evidence post-budget suggests that investors are enquiring more towards units that tend to have a higher yield and a lower entry point … compared to prior, when investors would be looking at houses that have stronger prospects of capital growth," Redman told SBS News.

Two places, Tasmania and the ACT, didn't see drops in investor interest — which Kusher said could be a sign they're moving toward properties with good rental returns relative to purchase...

title.en: 'Broken and grateful': Alice Springs farewells Kumanjayi Little Baby
title.zh: 爱丽丝泉告别库曼贾伊·小宝贝，现场“破碎而感恩”

summary.en: Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral in Alice Springs was marked by a solemn atmosphere, with speeches frequently interrupted by the heartfelt cries of those in mourning.
summary.zh: 库曼贾伊·小宝贝的葬礼在爱丽丝泉举行，现场气氛庄严肃穆，悼词不时被哀悼者的哭声打断。

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name and image of an Indigenous person who has passed away.

Alice Springs is known as the Red Centre of Australia but on 15 August, the community donned pink for the funeral of five-year-old Warlpiri girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby .

Warlpiri Elder and family spokesperson Robin Granites said pink was her favourite colour — it "reminds us of the clothes she used to wear".

"And the times when we would go in the evening, you see the sunset and even the early morning, you see the pink colour of clouds and that ... is a really good colour for us," Granites said ahead of the funeral.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Kumanjayi Little Baby's body was found on 30 April, after she went missing from Old Timers town camp, south of Alice Springs. Her disappearance sparked a five-day search, described as one of the largest search efforts in Northern Territory history.

47-year-old Jefferson Lewis has since been charged with her alleged murder and two other offences that cannot be published for legal reasons .

Pastor Rejeili Paulo-Smith spoke on behalf of Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother at the funeral service.

She requested that her daughter be remembered , "for who she was, not simply for the tragedy of how her life ended".

"Kumanjayi wasn't simply a little girl who was known by the community. She was Mum's baby too. She was a little girl whose presence filled their home and whose absence has left an enormous space," Paulo-Smith said.

It's been almost four months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby. During this time, her family and Indigenous communities have engaged in the grieving period and mourning process known as Sorry Business .

In recent months, Paulo-Smith said the community had felt "both broken and grateful".

"Broken because a precious little life has been taken from us far too soon, yet grateful because Kumanjayi Little Baby was here. She was known, she was loved, she mattered," she said.

The week following Kumanjayi Little Baby's death, thousands of Australians gathered at nationwide candlelight vigils.

At a local vigil in Alice Springs, 89-year-old Maya Cifali told NITV News the outpouring of community spirit was unlike anything she had ever seen.

"It is the first time that such a community spirit is felt for all of us," Cifali said.

Granites also believes the local community has displayed the Warlpiri concept of Jintangka; "which means we're all in one, everyone together".

At the funeral, he took the opportunity to thank Australians and people overseas for rallying behind his family during and in the months following the search...

reflection.en: The profound sorrow at Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral reminds us that grief is a natural and human response to loss. Even Yahweh, in human form, wept at the death of a friend, showing us that tears are a sacred expression of love and pain. In these moments, we find solace in knowing that our deepest sorrows are understood.
reflection.zh: 库曼贾伊·小宝贝葬礼上深沉的悲伤提醒我们，悲痛是对逝去之人的一种自然而人性的回应。即使是道成肉身的雅伟，也曾为朋友的离世而哭泣，这表明眼泪是爱与痛苦的神圣表达。在这样的时刻，我们因知道我们最深的悲伤被理解而得到慰藉。
